articles.text:
TKTMJ Wins $42.4 Million Army Corps Construction Contract In Louisiana
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 10:46 AM
TKTMJ Wins $42.4 Million Army Corps Construction Contract In Louisiana
TKTMJ has received a $42.4 million Army contract for construction and site work in Metairie, Louisiana. The Natchitoches, Louisiana-based small business will provide construction access to the work site, demolition, clearing and grubbing, excavation, embankment placement, geotextile and stone installation, and turf establishment and maintenance.
The firm-fixed-price contract was competitively procured through an internet solicitation. The government received four bids.
Work will be performed in Metairie and is expected to be completed by November 15, 2027. The contract is identified as W912P8-27-C-A003.
The full $42.4 million contract amount was obligated when the award was made using fiscal 2027 civil expenses funding.
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ New Orleans District is the contracting activity. The district oversees flood-risk management, navigation, coastal restoration, environmental, and other civil works projects throughout southern Louisiana.
Although the announcement does not name the specific project, the listed activities indicate a substantial civil construction effort involving preparation, earthwork, ground reinforcement, stone placement, and final site stabilization.
Construction access work will allow personnel and equipment to reach the active site. Demolition, clearing, and grubbing will remove existing structures, vegetation, debris, and other obstructions before excavation begins.
Excavation and embankment placement will reshape the site in accordance with the project design. Geotextiles can separate, reinforce, filter, or stabilize soil layers, while stone is commonly used for drainage, erosion control, structural support, or surface protection.
Turf establishment and maintenance will stabilize completed areas and restore ground cover after major construction activity.
The firm-fixed-price structure establishes an agreed amount for the defined scope, placing much of the performance-cost risk on TKTMJ unless the government authorizes changes.
Because the Army Corps obligated the entire amount at award, the $42.4 million represents a funded contract rather than an ordering ceiling or value dependent on unexercised options.

Promise Robotics Raises $40 Million CAD Series B to Scale the Production Infrastructure Powering Homebuilding
News provided by
Promise Robotics
Nov 17, 2026, 09:05 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Round led by White Star Capital follows a multi-year agreement with America's largest homebuilder and the launch of Promise's first U.S. facility in Phoenix.
PHOENIX , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Promise Robotics , the company bringing Physical AI to homebuilding, today announced the close of a $40 million CAD Series B funding round led by White Star Capital to expand the production infrastructure needed to scale homebuilding. The round also included participation from Horizons Ventures, Radical Ventures, Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments).
Homebuilders are under increasing pressure to expand housing production, but scaling through traditional construction methods alone is constrained by skilled labor availability and the complexity of adding production capacity market by market. Promise Robotics addresses that constraint by giving builders access to automated production capacity without requiring them to develop and operate factories themselves. The funding round will support the continued expansion of that production network across North America.
This announcement comes just weeks after Promise Robotics expanded its U.S. production network and signed a multi-year commercial agreement with D.R. Horton, America's largest homebuilder by volume. As the first major U.S. homebuilder to leverage Promise Robotics' Factory-as-a-Service® (FaaS) platform, D.R. Horton's adoption underscores growing demand for scalable, technology-driven homebuilding solutions. With production already live in Calgary and Nisku, Canada, more than 2,500 housing units under contract across three markets, and its first U.S. facility planned for Phoenix, the company is demonstrating the momentum and operating scale this new investment will help accelerate.
FaaS gives a broad range of homebuilders across geographies access to an integrated production platform that takes existing home designs and translates them into a coordinated production process spanning robotic manufacturing, factory operations, and onsite installation. Through FaaS, builders can access automated production capacity without developing and operating their own factories, helping them improve cycle times, increase capacity, and scale more predictably across communities and markets.
"Homebuilding can't scale on trade labor alone, and builders shouldn't have to become manufacturers to grow. We're building the production infrastructure the industry can scale on; a network of intelligent factories that get better with every home it helps build. This round lets us extend that network across North America," said Ramtin Attar, CEO and co-founder of Promise Robotics.
"From our very first conversations with the Promise Robotics team, it was clear nobody is building what they're building. Home construction is a massive industry that needs a new way to keep up with demand, and Promise is delivering it, giving builders automated production as a service through its technology, factories, and a business model designed to scale. articles.title: Spatial Intelligence Startup SE3 Raises $30M Series A Led by Accel
articles.snippet: Spatial Intelligence Startup SE3 Raises $30M Series A Led by Accel Wowtale
articles.text:
In a war zone where drones fly in large fleets, human operators cannot supervise every vehicle. When electronic warfare cuts off satellite navigation, each machine has to work out where it is and what surrounds it on its own. The EU aims to mobilise €800 billion in defence spending by 2030 and is planning a European Drone Wall to defend its eastern flank, which makes that kind of autonomy more valuable. A Munich startup working on this spatial awareness problem has raised a Series A.
SE3 combines computer vision and AI to turn sensor data into three-dimensional understanding so machines can decide and move on their own. It is developing the technology for environments where systems must keep working when satellite navigation is disrupted, and its immediate market is European defence.
The product is a spatial intelligence software layer for unmanned systems. It connects drones and ground vehicles from different manufacturers and fuses their sensor data into a shared 3D picture of the environment. It then adjusts behaviour, routes and positions for each vehicle in a swarm, and operators can command all functions by voice. The software runs entirely on the edge, so systems keep operating in contested environments.
SE3 also stresses that it is not tied to any one manufacturer’s vehicles. Modular procurement approaches such as MOSA and Germany’s MOSABw programme are making it easier for armed forces to combine systems from different suppliers, and the company sees growing demand for independent software that works across platforms without competing with the vehicles themselves.
In the past two years, SE3 has shipped thousands of systems, and it is working on multiple contracts with Ukraine and Germany’s armed forces, the Bundeswehr. It is an AI partner to defence primes including Rheinmetall and HENSOLDT and to scale-ups such as Auterion and ERC System. Auterion CEO Lorenz Meier said SE3’s spatial intelligence runs on Auterion’s Skynode, so customers get the capability on platforms they already operate, regardless of manufacturer.
SE3 spun out of the computer vision lab of Professor Daniel Cremers at the Technical University of Munich (TUM). Lukas Köstler is CEO and co-founder, and Simon Klenk is CTO. Both worked on PhDs in computer vision and robotics in that lab. Cremers is chief science officer, holds TUM’s chair for computer vision and AI, and won the Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize, Germany’s most prestigious research award.
SE3 announced the $30 million Series A on November 12. Accel led the round, with Keen , Lakestar and Seedcamp participating. Accel partner Matt Robinson said a team with talent from one of Europe’s leading research departments is well placed to build spatial AI for autonomous systems, a problem defence primes have found difficult.
The company will use the funds to grow its engineering, commercial and operations teams and fulfil further contracts. It plans to strengthen its presence in Germany and Ukraine, open a UK office and expand across Europe. Defence remains the focus, with robotics, emergency response and other civilian uses to be explored from 2027.
Capital Keeps Flowing to European Defence Startups
European defence startups have been raising large rounds. Helsing , Europe’s largest defence AI company, raised $1.8 billion in a Series E at an $18 billion valuation.
